record.paper_title: Recent developments and open problems in the theory of permanents
record.original_question: For an n x n doubly stochastic matrix A with all diagonal entries equal to 0, where doubly stochastic means that A has nonnegative entries and every row and column sums to 1, and where per(A) is the permanent of A, is per(A) minimized uniquely by the matrix whose diagonal entries are 0 and whose off-diagonal entries are 1/(n-1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ be an integer. Call an $n \times n$ real matrix $A = (a_{ij})$ doubly stochastic if $a_{ij} \geq 0$ for all $i,j$ and $\sum_{j=1}^n a_{ij} = \sum_{i=1}^n a_{ij} = 1$ for every $i$ and every $j$. The permanent of $A$ is defined by
$$\operatorname{per}(A) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \prod_{i=1}^n a_{i\sigma(i)},$$
where $S_n$ is the symmetric group on $\{1,\dots,n\}$. Let $\Omega_n^0$ denote the set of all $n\times n$ doubly stochastic matrices $A$ with $a_{ii} = 0$ for all $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$. Define $M_n \in \Omega_n^0$ to be the matrix whose diagonal entries equal $0$ and whose off-diagonal entries all equal $\tfrac{1}{n-1}$.

Prove or disprove: $\operatorname{per}(A) \geq \operatorname{per}(M_n)$ for every $A \in \Omega_n^0$, with equality if and only if $A = M_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the "zero-diagonal" analogue of the resolved van der Waerden conjecture (proved by Egorychev and Falikman) and is commonly stated as a conjecture in surveys on permanents. Web search did not surface a complete proof or disproof; the statement continues to be referenced as a conjecture, suggesting it remains open in general, although various partial and asymptotic results exist.

status_evidence.title: Doubly stochastic matrix — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Van der Waerden's conjecture states that the minimum permanent among all n × n doubly stochastic matrices is n!/n^n, achieved by the matrix with all entries equal to 1/n.
status_evidence.claim: The unconstrained version (van der Waerden) is solved; the zero-diagonal variant is a distinct, restricted problem.

status_evidence.title: Permanents of Doubly Stochastic Matrices (Troanca thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses conjectures on minimum permanent of doubly stochastic matrices with restricted patterns, including zero diagonal constraints.
status_evidence.claim: The zero-diagonal minimization remains discussed as a conjecture in the recent literature.
